method: Encodes and decodes the Linux open(2) flag word. The value table is the asm-generic/fcntl.h set as glibc exposes it on x86-64: O_RDONLY 0, O_WRONLY 1, O_RDWR 2, O_CREAT 0o100, O_EXCL 0o200, O_NOCTTY 0o400, O_TRUNC 0o1000, O_APPEND 0o2000, O_NONBLOCK 0o4000, O_DSYNC 0o10000, O_ASYNC 0o20000, O_DIRECT 0o40000, O_DIRECTORY 0o200000, O_NOFOLLOW 0o400000, O_NOATIME 0o1000000, O_CLOEXEC 0o2000000, O_SYNC 0o4010000, O_PATH 0o10000000 and O_TMPFILE 0o20200000. Encoding ORs the chosen access mode with each selected flag. O_SYNC already contains the O_DSYNC bit and O_TMPFILE already contains O_DIRECTORY, so each composite is reported once and the implied flag is folded out of the symbolic list rather than printed beside it. O_PATH is offered as an access mode because the kernel honours only O_CLOEXEC, O_DIRECTORY and O_NOFOLLOW alongside it, so any other selection is left out of the value and reported. Encoding marks the mode argument as required when O_CREAT or O_TMPFILE is set and warns when O_EXCL appears without O_CREAT, when O_TRUNC is combined with O_RDONLY, when O_TMPFILE lacks a write access mode, and about the alignment, ownership and descriptor-type conditions of O_DIRECT, O_NOATIME and O_ASYNC. Decoding reads hex after 0x and octal with an optional 0 or 0o prefix, refuses values above 32 bits and access bits of 0o3, names the private __O_SYNC and __O_TMPFILE bits when they appear without their companion bit, and reports bits that no flag on this ABI defines. The page models the numeric constants only: it does not model other architectures (O_DIRECT is 0o200000 on SPARC), umask, filesystem or mount behaviour, LSM or SELinux checks, kernel version differences, or the permission bits in the third mode argument, and it never opens, creates or inspects a file.
